companies.name: NextEra Energy
companies.role: Develops and operates power generation, renewable energy and storage; its utility delivers electricity to customers.

companies.name: GE Vernova
companies.role: Makes gas turbines, wind equipment and grid systems that expand electricity supply and delivery.

companies.name: Schneider Electric
companies.role: Supplies power distribution, energy management and automation, connecting the grid to data-center equipment.

companies.name: NVIDIA
companies.role: Designs GPUs and networking, and develops the software and systems that make accelerated computing usable at scale.

companies.name: AMD
companies.role: Designs Instinct accelerators and EPYC server CPUs, giving customers additional compute platforms.

companies.name: Broadcom
companies.role: Designs custom accelerators and networking silicon that connect large AI systems; also sells infrastructure software.

companies.name: TSMC
companies.role: Fabricates customers’ chip designs and provides advanced packaging, turning designs into manufacturable processors.

companies.name: Samsung Electronics
companies.role: Manufactures memory and logic chips, and offers foundry services; HBM supports high-bandwidth accelerator memory.

companies.name: Intel
companies.role: Designs processors and operates semiconductor fabs, including a foundry business for external customers.

companies.name: SK hynix
companies.role: Manufactures DRAM, NAND and high-bandwidth memory, helping accelerators keep data close to compute.

companies.name: Micron
companies.role: Manufactures DRAM, NAND and HBM; expands the memory and packaging supply that AI systems require.

companies.name: ASML
companies.role: Supplies lithography systems that print chip patterns on wafers, enabling foundries to manufacture advanced nodes.

companies.name: Vertiv
companies.role: Supplies power and thermal management to keep dense computing systems powered and cooled.

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.role: Operates Azure, provides model access and developer tools, and puts AI into work through Copilot applications.

companies.name: Amazon Web Services
companies.role: Rents cloud compute, designs Trainium chips and provides model access through Bedrock.

companies.name: Alphabet / Google
companies.role: Designs TPUs, operates Google Cloud, develops Gemini and integrates AI into consumer and workplace products.

companies.name: Meta
companies.role: Develops Llama models and applies AI to recommendations, advertising and consumer assistants.

companies.name: OpenAI
companies.role: Develops frontier models, sells API access and subscriptions, and provides ChatGPT for individual and workplace use.

companies.name: Anthropic
companies.role: Develops Claude models and tools such as Claude Code, supporting API use and enterprise workflows.

companies.name: Salesforce
companies.role: Integrates AI agents into customer relationship management, sales and service workflows through Agentforce.

companies.name: Palantir
companies.role: Connects organizational data to operational workflows and AI applications through its platforms and AIP.

companies.name: Marvell
companies.role: Designs custom compute ASICs, optical DSPs, SerDes, switching and storage silicon. Celestial AI adds optical scale-up interconnect technology.

companies.name: Credo
companies.role: Designs SerDes, optical DSPs and retimers, and supplies active electrical cables that preserve signal quality between high-speed systems.

companies.name: Astera Labs
companies.role: Supplies Aries PCIe retimers, Taurus Ethernet cable modules, Leo CXL memory controllers and Scorpio smart fabric switches to connect AI servers.

companies.name: Coherent
companies.role: Makes lasers, photonic devices and optical transceivers; develops optical engines and packaging approaches for co-packaged optics.

companies.name: Lumentum
companies.role: Supplies lasers and optical components and systems, including external laser sources for silicon photonics and co-packaged optics.

companies.name: Applied Optoelectronics
companies.role: Makes optical networking components and transceiver modules for data centers, alongside cable-broadband networking products.

companies.name: Fabrinet
companies.role: Provides precision optical packaging, assembly and manufacturing services for equipment makers, bringing complex optical designs into production.

companies.name: Corning
companies.role: Makes optical fiber, cable and connectivity for data-center networks; expands domestic manufacturing through long-term customer agreements.

companies.name: Amphenol
companies.role: Makes high-speed copper cables, connectors, fiber-optic interconnects and power connections that join servers, boards and racks.

companies.name: Arista Networks
companies.role: Builds Ethernet switching platforms and network software for AI and cloud clusters, turning networking silicon into managed systems.

companies.name: Cisco
companies.role: Designs Silicon One networking chips and builds switching systems; its Acacia portfolio supplies coherent optical connectivity.

companies.name: Celestica
companies.role: Designs and manufactures data-center infrastructure and advanced technology systems for customers, supporting hardware production at scale.

companies.name: Eaton
companies.role: Supplies electrical power-management equipment, including transformers, and expands manufacturing for utility, industrial and data-center demand.

companies.name: Quanta Services
companies.role: Builds and maintains electric power and other infrastructure, connecting engineering and skilled construction crews to grid and load growth.

companies.name: EMCOR
companies.role: Provides electrical and mechanical construction and building services, supplying the skilled installation and maintenance behind major facilities.

companies.name: First Solar
companies.role: Manufactures thin-film solar modules; domestic plants connect renewable generation supply chains to skilled manufacturing work.

companies.name: Lightmatter
companies.role: Develops Passage photonic interconnects and co-packaged optics. Its March 2026 disclosure describes chiplet sampling, not an installed fleet.

companies.name: Ayar Labs
companies.role: Develops TeraPHY optical I/O engines and SuperNova external light sources for optical links near compute chips.

companies.name: InnoLight
companies.role: Supplies high-speed optical transceiver modules that convert electrical data to optical signals for AI and data-center networks.

companies.name: Eoptolink
companies.role: Designs and manufactures optical transceiver modules, including 1.6T products for AI and cloud networks.

companies.name: Qcells
companies.role: Manufactures solar cells and modules, expanding the domestic solar supply chain through its Georgia factories. Part of Hanwha Solutions.

companies.name: Ciena
companies.role: Develops WaveLogic coherent DSP technology, optical transport and networking systems that connect data centers across distance.

companies.name: Semtech
companies.role: Supplies analog signal-integrity chips: laser drivers and transimpedance amplifiers for optical modules, plus CopperEdge equalizers for electrical links.

companies.name: MACOM
companies.role: Makes optical analog chips including laser drivers and transimpedance amplifiers, supporting transmit and receive functions inside optical modules.

companies.name: Tesla
companies.role: Develops FSD (Supervised), Robotaxi, Optimus and Cortex; Terafab co-developer. Customer FSD remains supervised.

companies.name: SpaceX
companies.role: Terafab co-developer and counterparty to Anthropic’s Colossus agreement. Parent company is distinct from the SpaceXAI business.

companies.name: xAI / SpaceXAI
companies.role: Grok model business and Colossus infrastructure under SpaceX. Contracted compute access is distinct from delivered model work.

companies.name: Waymo (Alphabet)
companies.role: Operates rider-only ride-hailing. Paid service, safety-driver testing and future launches remain separate. Alphabet revenue is not Waymo revenue.

companies.name: Oracle
companies.role: Supplies AI compute for named Stargate campuses used by OpenAI. Developer, chip owner and customer are distinct roles.

companies.name: SoftBank
companies.role: Stargate partner; Epoch identifies its chip ownership at Milam. Program commitments are not cash spent at every site.

companies.name: Vantage Data Centers
companies.role: Develops the Frontier campus in Shackelford County for Stargate; separate from Oracle chip ownership.

companies.name: Crusoe
companies.role: Develops Abilene data-center infrastructure supporting Oracle compute and OpenAI workloads.

companies.name: CoreWeave
companies.role: GPU cloud infrastructure for training and inference. Backlog is future contracted revenue, not commissioned MW.

companies.name: Nebius
companies.role: GPU cloud capacity; Microsoft contracted dedicated infrastructure at Vineland, subject to deployment and availability.

companies.name: Amkor
companies.role: Advanced packaging and test. Arizona construction supports a future domestic packaging chain; not current output.

companies.name: Super Micro Computer
companies.role: AI servers, racks and data-center building-block solutions, including liquid cooling. Revenue covers the whole company.

companies.name: Constellation Energy
companies.role: Nuclear generation and power contracts; Crane restart tied to Microsoft’s power-matching agreement and regulatory approvals.

companies.name: Memphis Light, Gas and Water
companies.role: Local utility distinguishes energized xAI service, new substations and requests requiring TVA approval.

companies.name: Tennessee Valley Authority
companies.role: Regional supplier and transmission approval authority in the MLGW–xAI power path.

companies.name: Agility Robotics
companies.role: Digit humanoids perform tote handling in commercial logistics. Contracts, completed tasks and fleet counts are distinct.

companies.name: Dell Technologies
companies.role: AI servers, storage, networking and integrated enterprise deployments; rack-scale liquid-cooled architectures. Product support does not prove shipments into a named campus.

companies.name: Foxconn / Hon Hai
companies.role: Builds and integrates AI server racks and modular data-center systems. Demonstrated platforms and potential collaborations are not installed customer capacity.

companies.name: Quanta Computer / QCT
companies.role: QCT supplies server, storage, networking and integrated rack solutions through parent Quanta Computer. Distinct from U.S. electrical contractor Quanta Services.

companies.name: Wiwynn
companies.role: Cloud server and rack integration, including cold-plate liquid cooling and serviceable liquid connections.

companies.name: nVent
companies.role: Data-center cooling infrastructure, including coolant distribution and heat-exchange systems. Vendor capability is not a named campus contract.

companies.name: CoolIT Systems (Ecolab)
companies.role: Direct liquid cooling for AI and high-performance computing. The company now identifies itself as part of Ecolab; stand-alone revenue remains unverified here.

companies.name: Johnson Controls
companies.role: Data-center thermal management, building controls, security and fire-protection systems.

companies.name: ERCOT
companies.role: Texas grid operator; verifies large-load interconnection requests. A queued project is not energized service.

companies.name: Fervo Energy
companies.role: Enhanced geothermal developer at Cape Station. Phase I commissioning and Phase II construction remain distinct delivery stages.

companies.name: Cognition
companies.role: Agent environment can write, run and test code with developer review. Vendor task-duration heuristics are not measured hours displaced.

companies.name: OpenClaw (open-source project)
companies.role: Self-hosted agent runtime connecting models and tools. Runtime availability and this site’s configured use do not imply widespread adoption or completed research.

supply_chain.title: Design
supply_chain.role: Architect the processor and its interconnects.
supply_chain.note: A chip designer may use an external foundry; cloud operators also design custom chips.

supply_chain.title: Fabrication
supply_chain.role: Pattern and process silicon wafers in fabs.
supply_chain.note: Foundry process, yield and available production slots matter alongside nameplate capacity.

supply_chain.title: Memory
supply_chain.note: HBM availability and qualification can limit complete accelerator supply.

supply_chain.title: Packaging
supply_chain.role: Connect compute and memory into a working device.
supply_chain.note: Advanced packaging is a separate production step. Foundry wafer starts do not measure packaging throughput.

supply_chain.title: Equipment
supply_chain.role: Provide the machines that make fabrication possible.
supply_chain.note: Lithography supports fabrication; additional equipment, materials and testing suppliers extend this chain.

employment.basis: Seasonally adjusted monthly payroll change; preliminary release, subject to revision.
employment.note: Broad sectors include activity unrelated to AI. These changes do not measure jobs caused or displaced by AI.

interpretation: The evidence supports an expansion of U.S. semiconductor and power-equipment manufacturing, with some production already operating. That is a concrete sign of industrial rebuilding. Project announcements and one month of employment data cannot establish a sustained economy-wide re-industrialization or net jobs attributable to AI.
gaps: No verified global total of usable AI accelerator capacity is available in this edition.
Comparable public HBM, advanced-packaging and optical-interconnect shipment series still need research.
Follow construction through equipment installation, qualification, production and sustained utilization.
Track realized permanent employment, wages, apprenticeships and local supplier activity over multiple years.
